cues.en: In order to achieve these
goals in the best possible way,
a good prompt should, of course,
include an instruction. That's
what you naturally add to
every prompt you're writing. If you, for
example, ask the AI to give you a
list of key advantages of using generative AI
versus Google, you got a pretty clear
instruction here and your goal obviously is to,
well, get such a list. That, of
course, is a perfectly valid prompt,
maybe not a great prompt, but it is a prompt and it might
get the job done for you. So, of
course, that's not something you need to learn, giving
the AI some instruction is, after all, the main
reason for using it in the first place.
Prompt engineering comes in when it comes to
fine-tuning that instruction and when it
comes to adding helpful
context that allows the generative
AI to follow that instruction in
the best possible way for your specific
task and goal. Now, helpful
context can mean things like
giving the AI a role,
which means that you add an instruction
like this to your prompt: You are an expert
LinkedIn marketer. Here, I'm assigning a
role to the AI. And the
idea, of course, is that I'm adding some extra
context, for example, that it's about
LinkedIn and that it's about marketing,
before I then write my actual
instruction so that my prompt is now
the instruction plus the extra
context, for example, a role here. But
it's not just about adding roles. It's
in general about adding
relevant information to your prompt,
so any extra
information that improves the
chances of the AI generating a
helpful response for you.
Because keep in mind, we're talking about a token
prediction machine here, you learned that
earlier in this course, so we wanna make
sure that this machine produces the
tokens, the words that
get the job done in the best possible way
for our specific task here. And
adding relevant information, of course, helps with that a
lot since in the end, the AI tries to complete the
sequence, so the more this sequence is
fine-tuned for our specific problem, the
better. That also includes
things like adding meaningful examples
and also maybe constraints.
For example, saying create a short
post already adds a little
constraint to this prompt, ensuring that we
don't get some super long post but
instead increasing the likelihood that
the response will be short, that we don't get
an overly long post.
So, put in other words, a good prompt
includes a detailed task description and
helpful context. Irrelevant information,
of course, must be avoided, so the idea is
not to add as much content and
text as possible to our prompt.
